title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your advanced Blueprint knowledge: data structures, timelines, delegates, interfaces, libraries, nativization, and best practices!

questions.question: Which collection type stores key‑value pairs?
questions.explanation: Map stores associations between unique keys and values.

questions.question: How do you access the first element of an array?
questions.explanation: Arrays are zero‑based; the first element is at index 0.

questions.question: A Set can contain duplicate values.
questions.explanation: Sets enforce uniqueness; adding an existing value does nothing.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Data Table?
options: Holding designer‑editable rows of structured data
questions.explanation: Data Tables import from CSV or manual entry, perfect for game data like items or dialogue.

questions.question: Which node is used to create animated value changes over time?
questions.explanation: Timeline provides curves that update per frame for smooth interpolation.

questions.question: How do you make a timer run repeatedly?
options: Call Set Timer again inside the function
Enable the Looping pin on Set Timer
questions.explanation: The Looping boolean input, when true, makes the timer call the function repeatedly.

questions.question: Latent nodes like Delay can be used inside Blueprint Functions.
questions.explanation: Latent nodes only work in Event Graphs and Macros, not in Functions.

questions.question: A Timeline's _____ pin fires continuously while it plays.
questions.explanation: Update outputs current track values each frame.

questions.question: Which delegate type allows multiple functions to be bound?
questions.explanation: Multicast delegates maintain a list of bound functions, calling them all.

questions.question: What must you do to prevent dangling delegate references?
questions.explanation: Always unbind delegates in EndPlay when the listener is destroyed.

questions.question: How do you pass data through an Event Dispatcher?
options: Add input parameters to the dispatcher
questions.explanation: In the dispatcher's Details, add inputs; they become payload variables.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of Blueprint Interfaces over Casting?
options: They allow communication without knowing the class
questions.explanation: Interfaces let you call functions on any actor that implements them, regardless of class hierarchy.

questions.question: How do you check if an actor implements an interface?
options: Use the Does Implement Interface node
Try to call the function and see if it fails
questions.explanation: Does Implement Interface returns true if the actor implements the specified interface.

questions.question: A Blueprint Function Library can store member variables.
questions.explanation: Function libraries are stateless; they cannot have instance variables, only static functions.

questions.question: What is a Blueprint Macro Library best used for?
options: Reusable graph snippets with multiple execution outputs
questions.explanation: Macros can have branching output flows, unlike functions.

questions.question: What does Blueprint Nativization do?
options: Converts Blueprints to C++ for better performance
questions.explanation: Nativization generates and compiles C++ code from Blueprint graphs.

questions.question: Which Project Setting enables nativization for all Blueprints?
questions.explanation: Inclusive converts all Blueprints; Exclusive only those marked.

questions.question: Nativization eliminates the need for C++ programming completely.
questions.explanation: It automates conversion but doesn't replace manual C++ for custom engine modifications or extreme optimization.

questions.question: Which practice reduces Blueprint Tick overhead?
options: Disabling Tick on actors that don't need it
questions.explanation: Tick consumes CPU every frame; disable it for idle actors.

questions.question: To keep Blueprint wires tidy, double‑click a wire to create a _____ Node.
questions.explanation: Reroute nodes route wires cleanly without changing logic.

questions.question: Why are naming conventions important?
options: They make the project look nice
They improve searchability and team clarity
questions.explanation: Consistent prefixes and names help everyone find and understand assets quickly.

questions.question: What prefix should a Widget Blueprint use?
questions.explanation: WBP_ is the standard prefix for Widget Blueprints.

questions.question: How can you view changes between two Blueprint versions?
questions.explanation: Unreal's Diff tool shows visual differences between binary Blueprint assets.

questions.question: Blueprint .uasset files can be merged automatically by Git.
questions.explanation: They are binary and cannot be auto‑merged; manual merging is required with special tools.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using Perforce for Blueprint collaboration?
questions.explanation: Locking files when editing prevents two people from modifying the same Blueprint simultaneously.

questions.question: Which loop type should you generally prefer for large arrays?
questions.explanation: For Each Loop creates a copy of each element; a standard For Loop with index is more efficient on large arrays.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Is Valid' node?
options: To check if an object reference is not null
To test if a function works
questions.explanation: Is Valid ensures a reference points to a valid object, preventing crashes.

questions.question: Where should you set a custom Category for functions in a Function Library?
options: In Class Settings of the library
questions.explanation: Class Settings has a 'Category' field that groups all functions under that name.
